eyebrow: T-SQL for Database Administrators · Chapter Ten
subtitle: Lesson 44 · Build Your DBA Toolkit

code:
SELECT
    r.session_id AS blocked_session,
    r.blocking_session_id AS blocked_by,
    r.wait_type, r.wait_time, r.wait_resource,
    t.text AS blocked_sql
FROM sys.dm_exec_requests AS r
CROSS APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(r.sql_handle) AS t
WHERE r.blocking_session_id <> 0
ORDER BY r.wait_time DESC;
caption: An empty result set here is good news — nothing is currently blocked.

eyebrow: Section 2 — the head of the chain
code:
SELECT DISTINCT r.blocking_session_id AS head_of_chain
FROM sys.dm_exec_requests AS r
WHERE r.blocking_session_id <> 0
  AND r.blocking_session_id NOT IN (
        SELECT session_id FROM sys.dm_exec_requests
        WHERE blocking_session_id <> 0
      );
caption: Blocking others, not itself blocked — this is the session to kill, not the end of the line.

code:
SELECT
    r.session_id, r.cpu_time, r.logical_reads,
    r.total_elapsed_time, r.blocking_session_id,
    t.text AS query_text
FROM sys.dm_exec_requests AS r
CROSS APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(r.sql_handle) AS t
WHERE r.session_id <> @@SPID
ORDER BY r.cpu_time DESC;
caption: Blocked and expensive on the same row is usually the most important line in the output.
